ops.text: the Legion stage: one Imperial shell (farmhouse01, thatch on plaster and rubble), door east onto the coast track; secondaryCultures imperial (0117 change set d6178109)
the net loft: a plank store west of the yard wall where the dry nets and rope are kept off the wet ground
the smokehouse: a second old stable, open on one side, by the track where the catch hangs in the smoke of a slow fire
the third household: a thatched plank house east of the home path, the newest of the salvage families

ops.why: The salvager household's work yard, trodden level with the house platform on its south side.

ops.text: each household works two spots. The sorting pile of barrels, crates and sacks stands by the door. The net-mending corner at the back holds the catch rack, the nets and the plank offcuts.

ops.why: The third household's sitting yard, trodden level beside the track on the house's north side.
The station-keeper keeps the stage door on the coast track, the office the families say they inherited.
The keeper sleeps in the stage, on a bedroll by its hearth.
The station-keeper watches the track from the stage door.
The merchant sells the week's salvage from the stall at the stage's north end.
Salvage lots are sold over the stall's counter.
The merchant's household sleeps in its house behind the tally table.
The families hang the salvaged rope and nets in the old stable to dry.
Nets and cordage dry on the rack in the yard.
The household sleeps in its house.
The timber stacks in the yard, each lot counted against its ship.
The stage door on the coast track.

ops.text: walk 12: the owner found the old stable empty; the recovered cordage (rope coils and nets) now lies in it, carrying fact why-occupantsMotive-2

walk 12: the owner saw nothing of wreck salvage; a salvaged ship's plank in the yard and a ship's anchor for sale by the stall show the trade (the Skyrim shipwreck boards are water-class and refuse dry ground)

walk 12: the held-back salvage (loot cache, tier 2) is a locked strongbox beside the old stable inside the locked yard (the stable floor is off the walk grid, so the box stands on the yard ground where a walker reaches it); the record's 'strongroom' is rewritten to this locked chest

lootTable.storyNote: Salvage held back from the count: the best of the last wrecks, kept out of the tally.

ops.why: The families keep back the best of each wreck from the hereditary count, locked in the stable.

ops.text: walk 12: the door lanterns stood under the plank porch overhang (base 0.29 m under the house); they now hang on the house wall by the door at 2 m (R127 wall host); ha/hb/nl alike

walk 12: the stage sold salvage with no board; the board hangs from the salvage stall's post by the stage (the stage's plaster wall is a 0.02 m shell, too thin for a hook under R127; serviceSignRule, R96)

ops.why: The board by the stage door names the old Legion stage and the salvage sold at the stall.

ops.text: walk 12: a stone cairn marks where the stage path leaves the main road (the turn-off stretch was bare; ground over 2 deg refuses sacks and planks); stands south of the path, clear of the paint
walk 12: a salvaged anchor beside the cairn tells a traveller on the main road that the turn-off leads to the wreck salvagers (openWayStretch dressing; the cairn is landscape and does not count)
